**My reasoning as this farmer:**

I have been farming this land for over fifty years. My father farmed it before me. Here in Quzhou, everyone grows wheat in the winter and maize in the summer — that is simply what we do, and I know these crops well. I have about 8 mu of contracted land. My son works in the city, so I manage it myself, though my back is not what it was.

I will plant winter wheat again this October on all 8 mu, then follow with summer maize on the same land after the wheat harvest in June. I do not experiment with other crops. Cotton prices have been bad, vegetables need too much work and water, and I do not know how to sell them. Wheat and maize I can sell easily at the village collection point.

For seed, I buy the improved wheat variety from the township supply cooperative — the same one I have used for several years. For maize I always buy hybrid seed, everyone does now, the yields are much better than the old kinds.

For fertilizer, I apply a full bag of compound fertilizer as base, then top-dress urea at jointing for wheat and at the big-bell stage for maize. I know researchers say we use too much fertilizer, but I worry about yield falling if I reduce it. Better safe than sorry.

I irrigate wheat four times — pre-winter, jointing, heading, and grain filling — because groundwater is available and I do not want to lose the crop to drought. Maize gets rain in summer so I only water twice, at emergence and if there is a dry spell in August.

I spray herbicide once before winter on the wheat, then aphid spray in spring, and maybe a fungicide if I see rust. For maize I spray for armyworm and weeds. I rotary till before wheat planting; for maize I sow directly into the wheat stubble without deep tillage to save time and fuel.
